A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TREC study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–J are available and support reliable matching despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original data-placement experiments, optimizer sweeps, MoE analyses, and 3.9B continual-pretraining results, including 578 measured TRECs documented in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including placement comparisons, TREC prediction scores, and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The TREC diagnostic, placement procedure, EMA-based predictor in Eq. (3), and power-law exponent model in Eq. (4) are unchanged. Added explanations and deployment advice introduce no new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SlimPajama blends and pretraining/CPT tasks, including code-placement tests and math-focused evaluation using OpenWebMath. Newly discussed SFT and grokking literature does not add evaluated tasks or datasets.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including general-blend and aggregate-blend training, alternative placement positions, and half/end/no-insertion CPT controls. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The description of Fig. 7 removes v1's erroneous '900B tokens' specification for the paired scratch/CPT runs, resolving a conflict with the 5-TPP comparison shown in both figures. This is a limited correction to the reported budget, not evidence of rerunning experiments; other settings and metrics match.

E4.justification: The placement-omission analysis, batch-size and momentum sweeps, schedule-history comparison, predictor ablations, and CPT failure analyses are retained. The new grokking discussion interprets existing evidence without adding an empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate and curve reporting practices. Neither adds repeated-seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched experimental plots and numerical tables retain their results. For example, v1 Tables 5–6 and v2 Tables 6–7 retain the 610M R² of 98.7% and TREC correlation of 98.4%; Fig. 10 retains the same CPT rankings. Reordered panels in Figs. 3 and 16 show the same curves.

T1.justification: Appendix F.3 replaces the small-weight-decay expansion with a derivation separating learning-rate scale from normalized coefficient shape. It also adds limiting arguments for vanishing learning-rate scale and large batch size. The central quadratic and minimizer-drift analysis in Appendix J is retained.

C1.justification: The introduction now explicitly qualifies the optimal-placement contribution as applying 'for a given optimizer configuration,' making the scope restriction more precise. The main claims about TREC predictability, scaling, and improved CPT remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation of order-dependent forgetting under i.i.d. sampling and proposes memorization versus grokking as an explanation for the cross-configuration generalization gap in Appendix D.2. Appendix A broadens the placement caveat from LR schedules to optimizer configurations and explicitly notes untested variation in placement reliability across data types.

D1.justification: New Table 1 gives explicit formulas for the existing placement-test LR schedules. Section 5.3 now identifies the empirical TREC from the vanilla CPT run as the basis for selecting placement. Architecture, tuning, hardware, training-time, and data-blend details were already documented.

R1.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B add Lesci et al. (2024), relating TREC to a final-checkpoint slice of memorisation profiles and distinguishing the controlled hyperparameter study and curriculum application. Other targeted additions cover grokking, plasticity, midtraining, and later scaling work.

P1.justification: Explanations are selectively expanded or rewritten, particularly in Section 2 and Appendices D.2, F.3, and G.4. Terminology and cross-references are refined, while the main section sequence and Appendices A–J retain their organization.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a document-wide Cerebras layout with different typography, margins, title treatment, running headers, copyright footers, and larger or repositioned displays. It adds the LR-schedule table and reorders and relabels panels in Figs. 3 and 16 while retaining their experimental content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the explanation of when placement guidance applies, acknowledges closely related memorisation work, and clarifies the normalized-coefficient limit in Appendix F.3. More explicit schedule and CPT documentation also helps readers. These are useful, limited gains; the empirical evidence remains unchanged, and the new grokking explanation remains untested.
